n.description: Number of items to be packed

assumptions.description: There is at least one item to pack.
Every item size is a positive integer that does not exceed the bin capacity.

code.python: assert all(1 <= l[j] <= W for j in range(n))

y.description: 1 if bin i is used, 0 otherwise

x.description: 1 if item j is assigned to bin i, 0 otherwise

constraints.description: The total size of the items assigned to a bin cannot exceed its capacity, and a bin can only hold items if it is used.
constraints.formulation: \sum_{j=0}^{n-1} l_j x_{ij} \leq W y_i \quad \forall i \in \{0, \ldots, n-1\}

constraints.description: Every item is assigned to exactly one bin.

objective.description: Minimize the total number of bins used.

code.gurobipy: model.setObjective(gp.quicksum(y[i] for i in range(n)), GRB.MINIMIZE)

notes: This is the classical bin-packing formulation attributed to Martello and Toth, presented in Section 1 of carvalho1999 (unnumbered equations, p. 630) as the starting point before introducing the arc-flow model of formulation `c`.

The source indexes bins and items by abstract sets without specifying the number of bins; following Martello and Toth, we take the number of bins to be n (the number of items), since $n$ bins always suffice, and index both bins and items directly over $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ rather than introducing separate named index sets.
The source works at the level of individual items (a list of $n$ item sizes), which is this dataset's canonical problem-level parametrization $(W, n, l)$ for p22.
